question: When someone used the fictitious name instead of his own name especially in writing is called?
solution:
The correct answer is **Pseudonym.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **pseudonym** is a fictitious name assumed by an individual, particularly an author, to conceal their identity.
 
• The term is derived from the Greek words *pseudes* (false) and *onoma* (name).
 
• In the literary world, a pseudonym is often referred to as a **pen name** or a **nom de plume**.
 
• Authors use pseudonyms for various reasons, including protecting their privacy, separating their personal lives from their professional work, or writing in a different genre than they are typically known for.
 
• Famous examples include Mark Twain (Samuel Clemens), George Orwell (Eric Blair), and J.K. Rowling (who used Robert Galbraith for crime fiction).

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Manuscript:** A book, document, or piece of music written by hand rather than typed or printed; it can also refer to an author's unpublished work.
 
• **Omniscient:** A term meaning "all-knowing." In literature, an omniscient narrator has a point of view that allows them to know everything about the characters and events in the story.
 
• **Ambidextrous:** A physical ability where a person is able to use both their right and left hands with equal skill and ease.
